hook: Adding boron-sulfur bonds speeds up OLED emitters and gives a device with 30.2% external quantum efficiency.
hook_turn: gives a device with 30.2% external quantum efficiency.

readout.label: External quantum efficiency of the OLED device

summary: Putting boron-sulfur bonds into narrowband OLED emitter molecules strengthens spin-orbit coupling, so spent energy states recycle into light faster (rates above 2.6 x 10^5 per second). It also made the borylation synthesis easier, with yields up to 85%. Results are from one emitter pair in a lab device, with no lifetime data in the abstract.
title: Incorporating B-S Bonds Into Multi-Resonance Frameworks for Narrowband Emitters With Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing and Facile Synthesis.
